---
title: "PPMI Proteomic Data Exploration based on UPDRS"
author: "Andrew Gumbert"
date: "September 2025 - April 2026"
output: html_document
---

Description:

This file  considers the UPDRS-based clusters from PPMI_UPDRS_Cluster_Creation.Rmd. The file also considers plasma, CSF, and urine proteomics data from Olink, SomaScan, and mass spectrometry. The code in this file acquires the numbers of cases with usable data from each type of proteomic modality. The file finds proteins that have relatively high differential expression by UPDRS cluster to identify candidate features for the creation of molecularly defined clusters. The resulting differentially expressed features are saved in text files, enabling further analyses and cluster creation.

### The following code blocks examine the plasma proteomics data from PPMI projects 9000 and 177.

##### The code uses the cluster assignments from the "PPMI_UPDRS_Cluster_Creation.Rmd" file.

```{r}
# gets PPMI plasma proteomic data from the combined panels (Project 9000)
proteomic_data_plasma_project_9000 <- rbind(read.csv(file.path(main_directory, "Proteomic_Analysis/PPMI_Project_9000_Plasma_Cardio_NPX_05Sep2025.csv")), read.csv(file.path(main_directory, "Proteomic_Analysis/PPMI_Project_9000_Plasma_INF_NPX_05Sep2025.csv")), read.csv(file.path(main_directory, "Proteomic_Analysis/PPMI_Project_9000_Plasma_NEURO_NPX_05Sep2025.csv")), read.csv(file.path(main_directory, "Proteomic_Analysis/PPMI_Project_9000_Plasma_ONC_NPX_05Sep2025.csv")))

length(unique(proteomic_data_plasma_project_9000$PATNO))


# filters to sporadic PD cases with cluster assignments at baseline
# Credit to https://www.digitalocean.com/community/tutorials/substring-function-in-r
# for help with the substring function.
proteomic_data_plasma_project_9000 <- proteomic_data_plasma_project_9000 %>% dplyr::filter(QC_WARNING == "PASS") %>% mutate(PATNO = substring(PATNO, 6, length(PATNO))) %>% dplyr::filter(PATNO %in% c(cluster_A_patients_overall, cluster_B_patients_overall) & EVENT_ID == "BL") %>% mutate(clust = case_when(PATNO %in% cluster_A_patients_overall ~ "A", PATNO %in% cluster_B_patients_overall ~ "B"))

# gets number of patients in the proteomic dataset with a cluster assignment
length(unique(proteomic_data_plasma_project_9000$PATNO))

```




```{r}
# checks how many cases with BL plasma proteomic data are in each UPDRS-based cluster
sum(unique(proteomic_data_plasma_project_9000$PATNO) %in% cluster_A_patients_overall)
sum(unique(proteomic_data_plasma_project_9000$PATNO) %in% cluster_B_patients_overall)
```



```{r}
# gets PPMI plasma proteomic data from Project 177
proteomic_data_plasma_project_177 <- read.csv(file.path(main_directory, "Proteomic_Analysis/PPMI_Project_177_Untargeted_Proteomics_24Oct2025.csv")) %>% dplyr::filter(TYPE == "Plasma")

length(unique(proteomic_data_plasma_project_177$PATNO))

# filters to sporadic PD cases with cluster assignments at baseline
proteomic_data_plasma_project_177 <- proteomic_data_plasma_project_177 %>% dplyr::filter(PATNO %in% c(cluster_A_patients_overall, cluster_B_patients_overall) & CLINICAL_EVENT == "BL") %>% mutate(clust = case_when(PATNO %in% cluster_A_patients_overall ~ "A", PATNO %in% cluster_B_patients_overall ~ "B"))

# gets number of patients in the proteomic dataset with a cluster assignment
length(unique(proteomic_data_plasma_project_177$PATNO))
```

```{r}
# checks how many cases with BL plasma proteomic data are in each UPDRS-based cluster
sum(unique(proteomic_data_plasma_project_177$PATNO) %in% cluster_A_patients_overall)
sum(unique(proteomic_data_plasma_project_177$PATNO) %in% cluster_B_patients_overall)
```



```{r}
# checks for total number of unique participants across the two plasma projects
unique_plasma_participants <- unique(c(proteomic_data_plasma_project_9000$PATNO, proteomic_data_plasma_project_177$PATNO))
length(unique_plasma_participants)

# checks how many cases with BL plasma proteomic data are in each cluster
sum(unique_plasma_participants %in% cluster_A_patients_overall)
sum(unique_plasma_participants %in% cluster_B_patients_overall)
```

### The following code blocks use wilcox tests to get pvalues and pvalue distributions for the baseline urine proteomic data

```{r}
# ensures all participants have at most one recorded result for each test
# credit to https://www.rdocumentation.org/packages/base/versions/3.6.2/topics/duplicated
# for help with the duplicated function
sum(!duplicated(proteomic_data_urine_project_190 %>% dplyr::select(PATNO, TESTNAME))) == nrow(proteomic_data_urine_project_190)
```


```{r, warning=FALSE}
# gets a list of test names from the urine samples
test_name_list_urine <- unique(proteomic_data_urine_project_190$TESTNAME)

# plots histogram of the distribution of how many cases correspond to each test
hist(sapply(1:length(test_name_list_urine), function(i){sum(proteomic_data_urine_project_190$TESTNAME == test_name_list_urine[i])}), xlab = "Number of Patients with Test Data", ylab = "Number of Tests", main = "Distribution of Numbers of Patients with Test Data for Each Test (Urine)")
abline(v = length(unique(proteomic_data_urine_project_190$PATNO)) * 0.9, col = "red")

# filters to only tests with < 10% missingness for downstream analyses
test_name_list_urine_low_missingness <- test_name_list_urine[sapply(1:length(test_name_list_urine), function(i){sum(proteomic_data_urine_project_190$TESTNAME == test_name_list_urine[i]) > (length(unique(proteomic_data_urine_project_190$PATNO)) * 0.9)})]

```

```{r}
# gets number of test names and those with low missingness and checks for uniqueness
length(test_name_list_urine)
length(unique(test_name_list_urine))

length(test_name_list_urine_low_missingness)
length(unique(test_name_list_urine_low_missingness))
```

```{r}
# uses the tests with low missingness to get pvalues and pvalue distributions from across UPDRS-based clusters
test_name_clust_pvals_urine <- sapply(test_name_list_urine_low_missingness, function(tn){wilcox.test(proteomic_data_urine_project_190[proteomic_data_urine_project_190$TESTNAME == tn & proteomic_data_urine_project_190$clust == "A" & proteomic_data_urine_project_190$CLINICAL_EVENT == "BL",]$TESTVALUE, proteomic_data_urine_project_190[proteomic_data_urine_project_190$TESTNAME == tn & proteomic_data_urine_project_190$clust == "B" & proteomic_data_urine_project_190$CLINICAL_EVENT == "BL",]$TESTVALUE)$p.value})

hist(test_name_clust_pvals_urine)

# credit to https://www.rdocumentation.org/packages/stats/versions/3.6.2/topics/p.adjust
# for help with the p.adjust function
test_name_clust_adj_pvals_urine <- p.adjust(test_name_clust_pvals_urine, method = "BH")

hist(test_name_clust_adj_pvals_urine)

protein_clust_test_results_urine <- data.frame(TESTNAME = names(test_name_clust_pvals_urine), pval = test_name_clust_pvals_urine, padj = test_name_clust_adj_pvals_urine) %>% arrange(padj)

# gets total number of proteins and checks for uniqueness
length(protein_clust_test_results_urine$TESTNAME)
length(unique(protein_clust_test_results_urine$TESTNAME))

# gets count and percentage of p-vals less than 0.05
sum(protein_clust_test_results_urine$pval < 0.05)
mean(protein_clust_test_results_urine$pval < 0.05)

# gets count and percentage of adj p-vals less than 0.05
sum(protein_clust_test_results_urine$padj < 0.05)
mean(protein_clust_test_results_urine$padj < 0.05)

```




### The following code blocks use wilcox tests for differential expression to get p-values and p-value distributions for the baseline CSF proteomic data (project 151)

```{r}
# ensure all remaining participants have at most one recorded result for each test
# credit to https://www.rdocumentation.org/packages/base/versions/3.6.2/topics/duplicated
# for help with the duplicated function
sum(!duplicated(proteomic_data_CSF_project_151 %>% dplyr::select(PATNO, TESTNAME))) == nrow(proteomic_data_CSF_project_151)
```


```{r, warning=FALSE}
# gets a list of test names from the CSF samples
test_name_list_CSF <- unique(proteomic_data_CSF_project_151$TESTNAME)

# plots histogram of the distribution of how many cases correspond to each test
hist(sapply(1:length(test_name_list_CSF), function(i){sum(proteomic_data_CSF_project_151$TESTNAME == test_name_list_CSF[i])}), xlab = "Number of Patients with Test Data", ylab = "Number of Tests", main = "Distribution of Numbers of Patients with Test Data for Each Test (CSF)")
abline(v = length(unique(proteomic_data_CSF_project_151$PATNO)) * 0.9, col = "red")

# filters to only tests with <= 10% missingness for downstream analyses
test_name_list_CSF_low_missingness <- test_name_list_CSF[sapply(1:length(test_name_list_CSF), function(i){sum(proteomic_data_CSF_project_151$TESTNAME == test_name_list_CSF[i]) > (length(unique(proteomic_data_CSF_project_151$PATNO)) * 0.9)})]

```


```{r}
# gets number of test names and those with low missingness and checks for uniqueness
length(test_name_list_CSF)
length(unique(test_name_list_CSF))

length(test_name_list_CSF_low_missingness)
length(unique(test_name_list_CSF_low_missingness))
```

```{r}
# applies a Wilcoxon test to each protein with low missingness across cluster A vs cluster B
test_name_clust_pvals_CSF <- sapply(test_name_list_CSF_low_missingness, function(tn){wilcox.test(proteomic_data_CSF_project_151[proteomic_data_CSF_project_151$TESTNAME == tn & proteomic_data_CSF_project_151$clust == "A" & proteomic_data_CSF_project_151$CLINICAL_EVENT == "BL",]$TESTVALUE, proteomic_data_CSF_project_151[proteomic_data_CSF_project_151$TESTNAME == tn & proteomic_data_CSF_project_151$clust == "B" & proteomic_data_CSF_project_151$CLINICAL_EVENT == "BL",]$TESTVALUE)$p.value})

hist(test_name_clust_pvals_CSF)

# credit to https://www.rdocumentation.org/packages/stats/versions/3.6.2/topics/p.adjust
# for help with the p.adjust function
test_name_clust_adj_pvals_CSF <- p.adjust(test_name_clust_pvals_CSF, method = "BH")

hist(test_name_clust_adj_pvals_CSF)

protein_clust_test_results_CSF <- data.frame(TESTNAME = names(test_name_clust_pvals_CSF), pval = test_name_clust_pvals_CSF, padj = test_name_clust_adj_pvals_CSF) %>% arrange(padj)

# gets total number of proteins and checks for uniqueness
length(protein_clust_test_results_CSF$TESTNAME)
length(unique(protein_clust_test_results_CSF$TESTNAME))

# gets count and percentage of p-vals less than 0.05
sum(protein_clust_test_results_CSF$pval < 0.05)
mean(protein_clust_test_results_CSF$pval < 0.05)

# gets count and percentage of adj p-vals less than 0.05
sum(protein_clust_test_results_CSF$padj < 0.05)
mean(protein_clust_test_results_CSF$padj < 0.05)

```



### The following code blocks get metadata and protein expression data of proteins meeting a signficance threshold to use in logistic regression and proteomic-based clustering.

```{r}
# selects proteins with p-vals less than 0.01 to use in downstream analyses from project 190 (urine)

urine_prots_meeting_threshold <- protein_clust_test_results_urine[protein_clust_test_results_urine$pval < 0.01,]$TESTNAME
length(urine_prots_meeting_threshold)


# gets data frames of baseline proteomic expression measurements 
proteomic_exp_data_meeting_threshold_urine <- proteomic_data_urine_project_190 %>% dplyr::filter(CLINICAL_EVENT == "BL") %>% dplyr::select(PATNO, TESTNAME, TESTVALUE) %>% dplyr::filter(TESTNAME %in% urine_prots_meeting_threshold) %>% pivot_wider(id_cols = "PATNO", values_from = "TESTVALUE", names_from = "TESTNAME") %>% arrange(PATNO) %>% column_to_rownames("PATNO")


# checks dimensions of resulting dataframe
dim(proteomic_exp_data_meeting_threshold_urine)

# gets number of patients in each longitudinal cluster
sum(row.names(proteomic_exp_data_meeting_threshold_urine) %in% cluster_A_patients_overall)
sum(row.names(proteomic_exp_data_meeting_threshold_urine) %in% cluster_B_patients_overall)
```


```{r}
# selects proteins with p-vals less than 0.01 to use in downstream analyses from project 151 (CSF)

CSF_prots_meeting_threshold <- protein_clust_test_results_CSF[protein_clust_test_results_CSF$pval < 0.01,]$TESTNAME
length(CSF_prots_meeting_threshold)


# gets data frames of baseline proteomic expression measurements 
proteomic_exp_data_meeting_threshold_CSF <- proteomic_data_CSF_project_151 %>% dplyr::filter(CLINICAL_EVENT == "BL") %>% dplyr::select(PATNO, TESTNAME, TESTVALUE) %>% dplyr::filter(TESTNAME %in% CSF_prots_meeting_threshold) %>% pivot_wider(id_cols = "PATNO", values_from = "TESTVALUE", names_from = "TESTNAME") %>% arrange(PATNO) %>% column_to_rownames("PATNO")


# checks dimensions of resulting dataframe
dim(proteomic_exp_data_meeting_threshold_CSF)

# gets number of patients in each longitudinal cluster
sum(row.names(proteomic_exp_data_meeting_threshold_CSF) %in% cluster_A_patients_overall)
sum(row.names(proteomic_exp_data_meeting_threshold_CSF) %in% cluster_B_patients_overall)
```



### The following code blocks examine and transform the urine proteomic data using the log function

```{r}
# checks for outliers in the urine measurements meeting the threshold
hist(proteomic_exp_data_meeting_threshold_urine[[1]])
hist(proteomic_exp_data_meeting_threshold_urine[[2]])
hist(proteomic_exp_data_meeting_threshold_urine[[3]])
hist(proteomic_exp_data_meeting_threshold_urine[[4]])
hist(proteomic_exp_data_meeting_threshold_urine[[5]])
```

```{r}
# checks for outliers in the CSF measurements meeting the threshold
hist(proteomic_exp_data_meeting_threshold_CSF[[1]])
hist(proteomic_exp_data_meeting_threshold_CSF[[2]])
hist(proteomic_exp_data_meeting_threshold_CSF[[3]])
hist(proteomic_exp_data_meeting_threshold_CSF[[4]])
hist(proteomic_exp_data_meeting_threshold_CSF[[5]])
```

```{r}
# normalizes the expression matrix with log transformation and scales it
proteomic_exp_data_meeting_threshold_urine <- scale(as.data.frame(apply(proteomic_exp_data_meeting_threshold_urine, 2, log)))

# gets fraction of missingness and imputes missing values with scaled mean of 0
mean(is.na(proteomic_exp_data_meeting_threshold_urine))
proteomic_exp_data_meeting_threshold_urine[is.na(proteomic_exp_data_meeting_threshold_urine)] <- 0
```


```{r}
# CSF data is already normalized. This code scales each feature to have a mean of 0 and SD of 1
proteomic_exp_data_meeting_threshold_CSF_processed <- scale(as.data.frame(proteomic_exp_data_meeting_threshold_CSF))

# gets fraction of missingness and imputes missing values with scaled mean of 0
mean(is.na(proteomic_exp_data_meeting_threshold_CSF_processed))
proteomic_exp_data_meeting_threshold_CSF_processed[is.na(proteomic_exp_data_meeting_threshold_CSF_processed)] <- 0
```


```{r}
# checks for rough normal distribution in the processed urine measurements meeting the threshold
hist(proteomic_exp_data_meeting_threshold_urine[,1], main = "Urine Proteomic Normality Test 1")
hist(proteomic_exp_data_meeting_threshold_urine[,2], main = "Urine Proteomic Normality Test 2")
hist(proteomic_exp_data_meeting_threshold_urine[,3], main = "Urine Proteomic Normality Test 3")
hist(proteomic_exp_data_meeting_threshold_urine[,4], main = "Urine Proteomic Normality Test 4")
hist(proteomic_exp_data_meeting_threshold_urine[,5], main = "Urine Proteomic Normality Test 5")
```

```{r}
# checks for rough normal distribution in the processed CSF measurements meeting the threshold
hist(proteomic_exp_data_meeting_threshold_CSF_processed[,1], main = "CSF Proteomic Normality Test 1")
hist(proteomic_exp_data_meeting_threshold_CSF_processed[,2], main = "CSF Proteomic Normality Test 2")
hist(proteomic_exp_data_meeting_threshold_CSF_processed[,3], main = "CSF Proteomic Normality Test 3")
hist(proteomic_exp_data_meeting_threshold_CSF_processed[,4], main = "CSF Proteomic Normality Test 4")
hist(proteomic_exp_data_meeting_threshold_CSF_processed[,5], main = "CSF Proteomic Normality Test 5")
```

```{r}
# writes a list of the selected proteomic features to export for cluster creation
writeLines(paste(colnames(proteomic_exp_data_meeting_threshold_urine), collapse = "\n"), file.path(main_directory, "selected_proteomic_features_urine_from_UPDRS_A_vs_B.txt"))
```


```{r}
# writes a list of the selected CSF proteomic features to export for cluster creation
writeLines(paste(colnames(proteomic_exp_data_meeting_threshold_CSF_processed), collapse = "\n"), file.path(main_directory, "selected_proteomic_features_CSF_from_UPDRS_A_vs_B.txt"))
```
